_readme: World of January 1st, 2016 ("Modern Day") — consumed by game.js's maybeApplyEraOverrides(), same as every other era_*.json preset, registered here for consistency/completeness rather than being a special-cased no-op.

Two-tier synchronization model (Stage 3): Tier 1 is this file's countryReassignments/regionReassignments — explicit historical-border rules for this era. Tier 2 is the canonical fallback: every shapeID this file does NOT explicitly reassign simply keeps its own real shapeGroup (its present-day sovereign owner, straight from the geoBoundaries source data) — which is exactly what Geo/era_modern.json (the master flat {shapeID: countryTag} lookup, generated by Scripts/mp1_build_era_modern.py) records for every shape in this game. No region or shape is ever left without an owner: Tier 1 overrides where explicitly listed, Tier 2 (the shape's own modern shapeGroup) covers everything else by construction.

This era has (by definition) no Tier 1 rules of its own — 2016 IS the modern baseline every other preset's countryReassignments/regionReassignments are diffed against. The handful of modern-day disputed-territory calls this project already makes (Somaliland split from Somalia, Western Sahara, etc.) are baked into defaultGameState()'s own provinceOwnerOverrides in game.js rather than duplicated here, since those apply regardless of which era is selected, not just this one.

Exists as a real, live preset (not dead weight) so 'Modern Day' participates in the exact same registered-preset system as 1911/1914/1936/1939 — see era:'modern' on the Modern Day entry in static/menu.js. Future explicit modern-era border changes (e.g. a newly-recognized state, a resolved border dispute) belong here, in countryReassignments/regionReassignments, the same way any historical preset's would.
